en: Abhidhānottara 6 = palm-leaf manuscript = Raghu Vīra’s manuscript reproduction by Lokesh Chandra
Now, therefore, I shall explain the secret: the unsurpassed mind-wheel.
One should place the most excellent of wheels in the center of the interior of the peaked pavilion—blue in color, of great brilliance, eight-spoked, and born from the secret.
In the center of that is a great lotus of universal colors with filaments,
renowned as having eight petals and being the seat for all the sons [of the Buddhas].
In its center is the moon, wherein resides Vajrasattva, the Great Bliss.
Having turned that away, one should recite the song arising from the deity, which is the true moon.

Hūṃ hūṃ āḥ! O Great Bliss! Alala hoḥ! O you who abide in union, through the application of supreme bliss, accomplish the Bodhisattva-bliss of the most excellent union! Hoḥ! O Lord of Union, consisting of bliss!

Oṃ hūṃ āḥ hoḥ! O Blessed One, Great Bliss, lift me up, lift me up! O you who consist of the most supreme bliss, hūṃ! Alalala hoḥ! You who abide in great bliss, possessing the bliss of the supreme net of the stainless moon of the highest joy!
Alalala! Hoḥ! He who consists of the bliss of supreme passion.

Immediately upon arising, together with his retinue, the Blessed One Mahāsukhacitta-Ḍāka appears—four-faced and twelve-armed, standing in the ālīḍha and pratyālīḍha postures, three-eyed and distorted, with faces that are blue, white, yellow, and red, terrifying with bared fangs; he embraces a vajra and bell, wears the severed head of Viṣṇu, and is supreme.

He has the body and four arms of Śiṣṭabhuja as described by Kāka, wears a garland of skulls, and bears a wreath of severed heads. He has a fierce girdle made of bound heads, a crown of Vajrasattva, and wears the crescent moon; his head is adorned with a double-vajra (viśvavajra), and he is clothed in a tiger skin. He is adorned with the six mudrās.
In front [of him] is Vajraḍākinī, who has one face, two arms, and three eyes;
her hair is loose, she is naked, and her girdle is decorated with fragments.
With his left arm he embraces a skull-cup, while in his right hand is a vajra and a threatening gesture;
with the joyful sounds of his girdle and waist-bells, which are as delightful as the sound of the Dharma,
[he proclaims] suchness, the limit of reality, emptiness, and the realm of phenomena.
By means of the drawing-in of the gnosis of equality, one should perform the cultivation of the ritual practice.
But when it is seen as perfectly pure, the yogin [perceives] that which is the most supreme of the supreme;
having made the Dharma of equal flavor, he should gaze upon his own wheel.
On the eastern petal is Ḍākinī, and likewise Rāmakī on the northern.
Khaṇḍarohā is in the west, and likewise Rūpiṇī is in the south.
White, yellow, red, and green—she is of the most excellent of colors.
She bears a skull and a khaṭvāṅga staff, as well as a ḍamaru drum and a curved knife.
She has three eyes, is deformed, naked, with disheveled hair, and terrifying in appearance.
Standing in the *ālīḍha* posture, she is intensely agitated by passion;
her face is slightly bashful with a side-long glance, and her breasts are full and elevated.
Her mouth is formidable with protruding fangs, and she is sealed with the five mudrās.
In the intermediate directions, four vases filled with the nectar of gnosis are placed;
having seen them, one sees skull-cups completely full, filled with the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).
On the eastern spoke of the mind-wheel (*cittacakra*), at Pullīramalaya, Khaṇḍakapālin and Pracaṇḍā are white;
on the north, at Jālandhara, Mahākaṅkāla and Caṇḍākṣī are yellow.
In Oḍiyāna in the west is Kaṅkālaprabhāvatī, who is red;
in Arbuda in the south is Vikaṭadaṃṣṭriṇamahānāsā, who is green in color;
and in Godāvarī in the southeast is Surāvairinavīramatī, who is as white as the sky.
In the southwest, at Rāmeśvarī, Amitābha’s Kharvarī is white and fair;
in the northwest, at Devikoṭa, Vajraprabhā’s Laṅkeśvarī is green;
in the northeast, at Mālava, Vajradeha’s Drumacchāyā is as pale as a lotus.
The Khecarī of the mind-wheel consists of the heroes such as Khaṇḍakapāla and others; they have one face and four arms,
wear crowns of matted hair and turbans, and are terrifying due to their fierce gestures.
With her two arms in an embrace, she holds a vajra and a vajra-bell;
in her left and right hands, she carries a khaṭvāṅga and a ḍamaru; her body is adorned with the five mudrās; and she stands in the ālīḍha posture.
Likewise, the goddesses beginning with Pracaṇḍā have one face and two arms; they embrace [their consorts] while holding skull-cups, brandish threatening gestures and vajras,
possess three eyes, have beautiful forms, and are resplendent with their hair loosened.
She is non-dual and absorbed in meditative equipoise, naked and overwhelmed by passion;
she wears necklaces, crest-jewels, armlets, earrings, garlands,
and the sacred thread, with a garland of heads adorning her neck and the jingling sounds of her girdle bells.
At the gates and in the corners are Kākāsyā and Yamadāḍhikā along with the goddesses;
their colors are exactly like those of the Ḍākinīs, and Kākāsyā and the others are likewise.
Likewise, one should meditate on the two beautiful forms of the Goddess stationed in Vidiśā,
who are of that same color and bestow all accomplishments;
having thus beheld the wheel of gnosis (jñānacakra), one should perform worship and consecration.
Having made all phenomena equal in flavor, one should take refuge in the state of selflessness.
The commitment of heart-knowledge, which accomplishes all desired aims,
is the supreme arrangement of body, speech, and mind, radiating a flood of Buddhas.
One should constantly observe the samaya and drink the water of the five nectars; through the yoga of worship and samaya, one should perform the recitation according to the prescribed rite.
Oṃ śrīcittaḍāka dhara āḥ khaṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ ḍākinījālasamvara svāhā. [Heart mantra]
Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ ha ha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. This is the near-heart mantra.
Oṃ vajraḍākinīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ sarvavajraḍākinīye vajravarṇanīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the heart mantra and the near-heart mantra.
Oṃ, to the ḍākinī, hūṃ 2 phaṭ!
Oṃ rāme hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ khaṇḍarohe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ rūpiṇīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, O you who hold a skull-fragment in your hand, act! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ pracaṇḍe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, perform it, O Mahākaṅkāla! Perform it, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ caṇḍākṣīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, bind the skeleton! Bind! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ prabhāvatī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, terrify, O you with formidable fangs! Terrify! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ mahānāse hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, agitate the enemies of the gods! Agitate! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vīramatī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ hrīṃ Amitābha hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ kharvarīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ hraḥ vajraprabha hraḥ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ Laṅkeśvarī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ haṃ vajradeha haṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ drumacchāye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O Kākāsyā, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O Owl-faced One, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, to the dog-faced one, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O sow-faced one, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ yamadāḍhī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ Yamadūtī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ Yamadaṃṣṭrī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ Yamamathanī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
One who possesses meditative cultivation should recite [the mantra] according to the sequence of emanation and reabsorption;
the practitioner of mantra will soon achieve success and attain the state of Vajrasattva.
He attains the perfection of mind, the supreme commitment of equanimity;
that great yogi shall wander at will and become the lord of those who move through the sky.
This entire triple world is established in the state of abiding;
at the time of arising, one should extract the six-limbed yoga.
Oṃ hūṃ; at the heart is white Vajrasattva.
Vairocana, yellow in color, is indeed upon the head.
Svāhā hūṃ: Padmanarteśvara, white as the moon, is at the crest-lock.
Vauṣaṭ! Hrīḥ! The armor is Heruka, white as the sky.
HŪṂ HŪṂ HOḤ: the Eye-Vajra-Sūrya, resembling the color of molten gold.
Phaṭ hūṃ; the weapon-mantra is in all limbs, and the supreme horse is greenish-white.
Oṃ vaṃ at the navel: Vajraḍākinī, sky-blue in color.
Hāṃ yāṃ, Yāminī is white in the heart.
Hrīṃ Moṃ: Mohanī, red in color, is in the mouth.
HŪṂ HRĪṂ: Saṃcāraṇī, yellow, on the head.
Hūṃ hūṃ; at the crest-lock is Saṃtrāsanī, who is blue.
"Phaṭ 2! Caṇḍikā, the weapon in all limbs, red and crimson"—with this, one should roam at ease as one pleases.
One should contemplate the entire world according to the ritual procedure through the vajra-knot;
by means of this non-dual yoga, one becomes all phenomena.
"Free from possessiveness, free from ego, free from appearance, and free from syllables. Thus ends the third chapter, on the Vows and the Guru’s Lineage, in the *Abhidhānottara*.
